lyrics-block.comment: Inside lyrics { … } the words are syllables, not code, so reserved words like 'key'/'time'/'a'/'f' must NOT be highlighted as keywords or pitches. Match the block as its own context that only knows comments, quoted syllables, barlines and the connector tokens; everything else stays plain text. The part-major form `lyrics { section A { … } }` nests one level: #lyrics-inner-section colours the section keyword+name AND balances its braces so this block doesn't end at the inner '}'.

lyrics-inner-section.comment: Part-major lyric track: `section NAME { … }` written inside lyrics { }. Colour the section keyword and its name; the body is more lyric syllables, and matching the inner braces keeps the outer lyrics block from ending at this section's '}'.

lyrics-content.comment: The syllable-safe inner tokens of a lyrics block: comments, quoted syllables, barlines and lyric connectors. Everything else stays plain text (a syllable).

patterns.comment: Lyric connectors: hyphen (--), extender (__ or _), melisma (~)
patterns.name: punctuation.separator.lyric-connector.lilysharp

fonts-block.comment: `fonts { serif "Georgia"  barNumber sans }`. ⚠️ The KEYS are a vocabulary of their own (LilySharp.Core TextRole.AllKeySpellings) and are NOT reserved words — `part barNumber { … }` compiles — so nothing outside this block may colour them, and only a rule that knows it is INSIDE one can. That is what begin/end is for: it carries CONTEXT, which is a claim about what a word IS. (It is not licence to claim a word is WRONG; see the #keywords comment.) A key the parser knows and this list omits comes out plain, which is what `serif`/`sans`/`barNumber` did until 2026-08-18 while `tempo` next to them was coloured — by the keyword rule, for an unrelated reason. EditorColouringTests holds this list to TextRole.AllKeySpellings in both directions.

patterns.comment: A key POINTED AT a generic family instead of a face name: `marks sans`, `serif sans`. Read before the bare-key rule so the second word is seen as the value it is. ⚠️ `sans-serif` precedes `sans` in both lists — TextMate takes the first alternative that matches, and \b succeeds before the hyphen, so the shorter spelling would colour `sans` and leave `-serif` plain (the same trap #instrument-value was written for).
The one entry that is a bare word rather than a key/value pair, and the one word here that IS reserved.
patterns.name: keyword.other.lilysharp

paper-block.comment: `paper { paperWidth 210mm  systemSystemSpacing { basicDistance 12 } }`. Same device as #fonts-block and for the same reason: the KEYS are a vocabulary of their own (LilySharp.Core LanguageVocabulary.PaperScalarKeys / PaperSpacingKeys / PaperSpacingSubKeys) and are NOT reserved words — `part indent { … }` compiles — so only a rule that knows it is INSIDE the block may colour them. The nested spacing block is its OWN begin/end so that its `}` does not close the outer region early. A number's GLUED unit (210mm — one quantity) is coloured with its number by #paper-length; the units are not reserved either. EditorColouringTests holds these lists to LanguageVocabulary in both directions.

patterns.comment: A spacing key still gets its colour while the writer has typed it and not yet its `{` — the begin rule above takes over the moment the brace lands.
patterns.name: keyword.other.paper-key.lilysharp

paper-length.comment: A paper value: a number with its optional GLUED unit — `210mm` is one quantity, so the unit is coloured with its number (captures, like a directive value, never a bare alternation: mm/cm/in are free words everywhere else).

part-body.comment: `part vln1 "Violin I" { clef treble^8  tuning standard  removeEmpty all }`. ⚠️ These are the part header's OWN vocabulary (LilySharp.Core SymbolCaseValidator) and almost none of them is a reserved word — `part lines { … }`, `part bracket { … }` and `part standard { … }` all compile (measured 2026-08-19) — so nothing outside this block may colour them and only a rule that knows it is INSIDE one can. Same device as #fonts-block and for the same reason: begin/end carries CONTEXT, which is a claim about what a word IS, not licence to claim a word is WRONG. ⚠️ The vocabulary is the PART BODY's, not the language's everywhere: a body takes all eleven clef names while `clef` in music and `staff` in a score take five and refuse the other six (measured). Each value is read WITH the key it belongs to, so `tuning treble` does not come out looking like a tuning — wrongness is the diagnostics'. EditorColouringTests holds every list here to its Core set in both directions.

patterns.comment: ⚠️ Longest spelling first, in every list below: TextMate takes the first alternative that matches and \b succeeds before `_` is not true — but it DOES succeed before `^`, so a bare `treble` would colour the head of `treble^8` and leave `^8` plain. `treble_8`/`bass_8` are the same trap with the boundary inside the word.

⚠️ `15ma`/`15mb` before `8va`/`8vb` is not a prefix question here — they share no head — but the list is written longest-first like the others so the file has one habit. The marker is a value, not a keyword: `part transposition { … }` compiles.
The bare key, read AFTER every key/value pair above so the pair wins and the value is scoped as the value it is. `transposition` precedes `transpose`, which is a prefix of it.
patterns.name: keyword.other.lilysharp

tab-tuning.comment: `score main { tab guitar melody }`. The ONE position a tuning name reaches outside a part body (measured 2026-08-19: all seven are accepted after `tab`, and `staff`/`ossia` take clef names, not tunings). Without this the vocabulary would be coloured in the header and plain in the score — the same half-coloured shape the user reported for `fonts { }`.

patterns.comment: The preset after 'instrument' is ONE hyphenated word ('electric-bass', 'double-bass'). Highlight the whole name — without this, the generic keyword rule colours only the trailing 'bass' segment and leaves 'electric-' plain. A quoted display label (instrument violin "1st Violin") is left to the string rule.

directive-value.comment: A directive and the ONE word that is its value: `octave relative`, `repeat unfold 2`. ⚠️ The value words are NOT reserved — `part relative { … }` and `part unfold { … }` both compile (measured 2026-08-18) — so colouring them from a bare alternation paints a writer's own part name as a keyword. Same device as #instrument-value, and it has to be included BEFORE #keywords so the two-word form is read first.

keywords.comment: ⚠️ THIS FILE MAY SAY WHAT A WORD IS, AND MAY NOT SAY THAT IT IS WRONG. A rule here sees one line and no position, so it cannot tell a dead spelling from a live one: `repeat volta 2` is removed (LYS0006) while `fonts { volta "TeX Gyre Schola" }` is accepted, and one regex holds nothing that separates them. Errors travel as diagnostics, which are anchored to a span — user decision 2026-08-18, ratcheted by EditorColouringTests.TheGrammarCallsNothingInvalid. ⚠️ The words below are held to Lexer.GetKeywordKind by that same file: a reserved word a writer can type and no pattern here matches is a word the editor leaves plain (23 of them were, until 2026-08-18). A spelling that is NOT reserved is equally a defect. The '_8' clefs and 'tocoda' are written before their shorter twins so the longer spelling is read whole.

patterns.comment: Navigation marks, written bare in a form block: 'A dc al fine', 'to coda', and the run-together 'tocoda'.
patterns.name: keyword.control.navigation.lilysharp

patterns.comment: Inline volta endings: [1. ...] [2. ...] [1-3. ...] [1,3. ...] — '[' + number disambiguates volta vs beam

patterns.name: variable.other.pitch.lilysharp
patterns.comment: A slash note: '/' in note position (rhythm notation). Not preceded by a word character, so `time 4/4`, `tuplet 3/2` and a chord entry's `c/g` keep their own '/'.

patterns.name: variable.other.pitch.lilysharp
patterns.comment: Accidentals: is/es (sharp/flat), isis/eses (double), isih/eseh + ih/eh (quarter-tones) — the lexer produces no 'as'. Trailing (?![A-Za-z]) so a pitch letter that merely starts a longer word (g in grandStaff, b in bass, c in clef) is NOT mis-highlighted as a note.
@-prefixed dynamics ('f' bare is a PITCH; @f is the dynamic). Backslash dynamics (\p, \f) are rejected by the parser — not highlighted as valid.
patterns.name: keyword.other.dynamic.lilysharp

patterns.comment: Value-carrying annotations take PARENTHESES: @mark(A), @fig(6 4), @chord(Dm), @feather(right), @ped(off), @text("dolce"), @tuplet(3), @finger(1), @bend(…), @notehead(…), @frame(…). (The old dotted form @mark.A / @fig.6.4 was removed.)
Plain @name annotation: articulations, ornaments, dynamic text, spanners, navigation marks (@segno/@coda/@fine/@rit…), and any @name-registry name — all resolved from text, so always colored.
patterns.name: keyword.other.annotation.lilysharp
keyword.other.articulation.lilysharp
patterns.comment: Keep in sync with LilySharp.Core ArticulationRegistry (full names + abbreviations).
